questions.concept: Mutable list inside a tuple can be changed
questions.question:
What is the output of the following code?
t = (10, 20, [30, 40])
t[2][0] = 35
print(t)
questions.explanation: The tuple itself cannot be changed, but its element at index 2 is a mutable list, which can be modified in place.

questions.question: A developer wants more gap between neighbouring cells of a table, without changing the gap between each cell's text and its own border. Which property should be increased?
questions.explanation: Cell spacing is the space between adjacent cells, while cell padding is the space between cell content and its border.

questions.question: Which component executes Java bytecode during the run phase?
questions.explanation: The JVM executes the bytecode in .class files. javac only compiles source to bytecode and jdb is a debugger.

questions.question: The microprocessor belongs to which generation of computers?
questions.explanation: Microprocessors (from LSI/VLSI chips) mark the 4th generation of computers. Third generation used integrated circuits.

questions.question: Which microcontroller is used in the Arduino UNO?
questions.explanation: The Arduino UNO uses the ATmega328p microcontroller; ATmega2560 is used on the Arduino Mega.

questions.question: Contention-based MAC protocols are commonly used in which type of network?
questions.explanation: Ethernet nodes contend for the shared medium; Token Ring uses token passing instead of contention.

questions.concept: No separate character data type in Python
questions.question: How does Python represent a single character such as 'A'?

options.A: As a separate char data type
options.B: As an int holding its ASCII value
options.C: As a string of length one
options.D: As a tuple with one element

questions.explanation: Python has no character data type; a single character is simply a string of length one.

questions.concept: Data redundancy as duplication of same data
questions.question: A school keeps the guardian's name and phone number both in the STUDENT file and in a separate fee file. Which file-system limitation does this duplication of the same data in different places represent?
questions.explanation: Data redundancy means the same data is duplicated in different places, which wastes storage and can lead to inconsistency.

questions.question: An IPv4 address with first octet 245 belongs to which class?
questions.explanation: Class E covers 240-254 and is reserved for experimental use; Class D is 224-239.

questions.question: In an output-restricted dequeue, which operations are allowed?

options.A: Insertion at both ends, no deletion
options.B: Insertion and deletion at only one end
options.C: Deletion at only one end, insertion at both ends
options.D: Insertion at only one end, deletion at both ends

questions.explanation: Output-restricted means deletion (output) is limited to one end while insertion can be done from both ends. The reverse describes the input-restricted dequeue.

questions.question: In the six-tuple definition of a Moore machine, what does lambda denote?
questions.explanation: Lambda is the output transition function; O/A is the output alphabet and delta the state transition function.

questions.question: A web application is checked to ensure it runs correctly on Chrome, Firefox and Edge across Windows and Linux. This is:
questions.explanation: Browser compatibility testing ensures a web application runs on different browser and operating system combinations. Backward compatibility concerns older versions' files and environments.

questions.concept: pickle.dump() needs file opened in wb mode
questions.question: Which statement correctly opens a file for writing a list with pickle.dump()?
questions.explanation: pickle writes byte streams, so the file must be opened in binary write mode, 'wb'. 'rb' is used when loading.

questions.concept: Count of edge entries in undirected adjacency matrix
questions.question: An undirected graph has vertices A, B, C, D and edges A-B, B-C and C-D. In its adjacency matrix (1 for an edge, 0 otherwise), how many entries are 1?
questions.explanation: In an undirected graph each edge appears at both (u, v) and (v, u), so 3 edges give 6 entries of 1.

questions.question: Which IoT protocol is used for scalability and modularity and offers guaranteed message delivery?
questions.explanation: AMQP (Advanced Message Queuing Protocol) provides scalability, modularity and guaranteed message delivery, and processes messages into queues.

questions.concept: Major functions of an operating system
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT listed among the major functions of an operating system?
questions.explanation: The major OS functions are job accounting, process management, file management, networking, device management and security. Compiling source code is the job of a language translator.

questions.question: SQL injection is best described as:

options.A: malware that encrypts a database and demands ransom
options.B: a protocol used to secure database connections
options.C: a method of capturing small packets on a network
options.D: a code injection technique used to attack data-driven applications

questions.explanation: SQL injection is a code injection technique used to attack data-driven applications; packet capture is sniffing and ransom demands are ransomware.

questions.question: Three T flip-flops (each in toggle mode) are cascaded, with the output of each driving the clock of the next. If the first receives a 16 kHz clock, what is the output frequency of the third?
questions.explanation: Each T flip-flop halves the frequency: 16 to 8 to 4 to 2 kHz. Dividing by 3 instead of 2^3 is a conceptual mistake.

questions.question: In the flow Source code -> Translator -> Object code -> ____ -> Execution, which component fills the blank?
questions.explanation: Compilers, assemblers and interpreters produce object code, which the loader places into memory for execution.

questions.question: Who is known as the father of the relational database?
questions.explanation: E. F. Codd is the father of the relational database; Charles Bachman created the first DBMS (IDS).

questions.question: The elements 34, 16, 2, 93, 75 and 40 are stored in an empty hash table of 10 positions using h(element) = element % 10. How many positions remain empty?
questions.explanation: The indices used are 4, 6, 2, 3, 5 and 0, all distinct, so 6 of the 10 positions are filled and 4 remain empty.

questions.question: A malicious program looks like a legitimate game and tricks a user into installing it, but it does not copy itself or infect other files on its own. It is best classified as a:
questions.explanation: A Trojan looks like legitimate software and tricks users into installing it, but it does not self-replicate or infect other files by itself, unlike worms and viruses.

questions.concept: Intersection listed for regular but not context-free languages
questions.question: Which operation is listed for Regular Languages (Type 3) but NOT for Context-Free Languages (Type 2)?
questions.explanation: Union, Kleene star and Kleene plus are listed for both classes, while intersection is listed only for regular languages.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an open-source operating system?
questions.explanation: Fedora, Debian and Gentoo are listed open-source operating systems; Windows is proprietary.

questions.question: Online shopping was pioneered in 1979 in the United Kingdom by:
questions.explanation: Michael Aldrich pioneered online shopping in 1979; Tim Berners-Lee created the WWW and Bob Goldstein coined multimedia.
